name: spec
description: Spec pipeline v7 — a small code program run by a trusted engineer, verified by executed evidence. Lifecycle: /spec:genesis (greenfield) → roadmap briefs → /spec:mocks → /spec:plan → /spec:run (build, then review, each driver-stepped with one fresh-context reviewer and a derived verdict) → /spec:release; plus /spec:status, /spec:doctor, /spec:enforce, /spec:fix. Changelog (last 3): 7.338.0 — Fan-out has two modes: the bare run is AUTO (derived batch, boundaries, the pending queued fixes and red-CI rows always tabled as the fix group, one 📌 line, no question) and `--pick` is SELF-PICK (a checkbox round, one --label per ticked box, the same boundary validation). Removed flags: `--batch`, `--include-fixes`, `--override-serial`, `--ask`, `--lanes`, and positional spec paths; the per-run ask overlay is retired (set the stops key to ask instead) and the grounding contract drops its --ask clause. no dependency change. 7.337.0 — Fan-out lanes now run in parallel whatever files their File Plans share; the MERGE step rebases each lane onto main and fast-forwards it, a conflict sends the lane back to its worker to resolve by intent and it lands on the next pass, and a second conflict against the same main stops the lane for a person. The batch boundaries are deleted (no more stopping at a spec touching pipeline files or sharing a risk-tier file), and so is the policy fanout block with its self-surface globs and exempt list. No dependency change. 7.336.0 — The legs seal the manifest: one shared manifest reader (lib/manifest.js) keeps the first row per leg and reports a duplicate leg as invalid evidence; the review driver records a digest of each manifest its legs run wrote and refuses every later invocation on drift, naming the cause and the rm-and-rerun remedy; the reviewer and disposer re-run a leg only against a scratch copy.
